subject: Clarify transient data escrow & deletion schedule

From: Grace Lin <grace.lin@lumina-analytics.com>

Cc: procurement@lumina-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient data escrow / deletion timeline questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo this week — the performance numbers looked very promising. Before we move to signature, procurement asked us to clarify one bespoke item: Lumina wants an explicit transient/escrow window for query-level logs that contain PII when using your hosted inference. Specifically: how long will query-level traces be retained in the event of an incident, and what is the guaranteed deletion timeline after account termination?

A few concrete asks from their side:
- Maximum retention for query traces that include PII — requested range: 7–30 days.
- A clear process and timeline for secure deletion after termination (they'd like deletion and certificate within 30 days).
- Any conditions where you would retain snapshots for debugging or legal hold.

Can you confirm what Redwood can commit to in the order form versus what's our internal default? We need language that procurement can sign off on.

Appreciate it — Grace
Grace Lin
Head of Platform Compliance, Lumina Analytics
(415) 555-0123

(Attachment: Lumina_Reqs_May2027.xlsx [application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet])

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Grace Lin <grace.lin@lumina-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Transient data escrow / deletion timeline questions

Thanks Grace — great questions. Short answer: we can propose a bespoke retention window in the order form and a certified deletion timeline; the details depend on whether you use Hosted (shared) vs Dedicated capacity.

High-level proposal for the order form (what we can commit to):
- Hosted API (shared): ephemeral query logs retained up to 14 days by default; we can constrict to 7 days as a contractual limit.
- Dedicated: we can contract a 0–7 day window for query-level traces if Lumina requires more aggressive limits, plus an explicit certification of deletion within 14 days of termination.
- For both modes, aggregated telemetry without customer identifiers is retained for 12 months for service health unless otherwise specified.
- Exceptions: legal hold or a court order would supersede standard deletion timelines.

Next steps I propose: I’ll loop in Marissa (Legal/Orders) to draft the exact order form wording and Neha on engineering to confirm the deletion certification mechanism (certificate + logs describing action taken). If that sounds good I’ll send a redline and a draft deletion playbook.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi — did some digging with infra and platform ops. Summary of what we can produce today and what would require engineering changes:

What we can commit to in the order form with current platform:
- Dedicated customers: we can guarantee:
  - Query-level traces containing PII will be retained no more than 7 days on disk.
  - On termination of Dedicated capacity, a targeted wipe of the tenant GPUs and associated caches completes within 7 business days; we will provide a deletion certificate signed by the security lead.
- Hosted customers (shared):
  - Default ephemeral traces retention is 14 days. We can offer a contractual cap of 7 days but that requires a configuration change that would apply to your tenant and be irreversible for the contract term.
  - Deletion after termination: full logical deletion and metadata scrubbing occurs within 14 business days; physical snapshot purging may take longer depending on backup windows. We can commit to a deletion certificate within 14 business days.

What would require product work (timeline estimate):
- Providing a per-customer automatic 7 day cap for hosted without an irreversible config flip: 4–6 weeks (engineering change).
- An on-demand one-click deletion cert job in Console: 3–5 weeks.

Recommended order form wording (draft):
"Customer may elect Dedicated or Hosted service. For Dedicated service Redwood will retain query-level traces containing customer identifiers no longer than seven (7) days and will complete deletion and provide a signed deletion certificate within seven (7) business days after termination. For Hosted service Redwood retains query-level traces for up to fourteen (14) days by default; upon Customer election Redwood will limit retention to seven (7) days for the duration of the Term; Redwood will complete logical deletion and provide a signed deletion certificate within fourteen (14) business days after termination. Exclusions: legal hold, court order, or required retention under applicable law."

Happy to refine once Marissa weighs in on legal phrasing.

— Neha
Platform Security
Redwood Inference
